question: What is the main goal of pharmacovigilance?

options.A: The process of pricing essential medicines for hospitals
options.B: The clinical trial phase before a drug gets approved
options.C: The study of detecting and preventing adverse drug effects
options.D: The science of manufacturing safe herbal medications

explanation: Pharmacovigilance centers entirely on monitoring, assessing, and preventing harm caused by pharmaceutical products after release. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why do we still need to monitor drugs even after they pass clinical trials?

options.A: Government agencies ban drugs after five years automatically
options.B: Patients always alter their prescribed dosages at home
options.C: Clinical trials use small populations and miss rare adverse events
options.D: Pharmaceutical companies demand constant safety updates for profit

explanation: Pre-approval trials cannot reveal every side effect that might appear in diverse, large populations over long periods. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which historical drug disaster led to severe birth defects and changed global drug safety laws?
explanation: The thalidomide tragedy exposed severe gaps in prenatal drug safety and catalyzed modern global pharmacovigilance systems. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h2)

question: What major change in healthcare happened because of past drug disasters?

options.A: Mandatory testing and systematic post-market drug surveillance
options.B: Free distribution of all prescription drugs to patients
options.C: Removal of clinical trials from the drug approval process
options.D: Complete elimination of side effects in new medications

explanation: Past tragedies forced regulatory authorities to establish rigorous pre-clinical testing and ongoing post-market monitoring frameworks. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which type of adverse drug reaction depends on the dose and can be predicted?
explanation: Type A reactions are augmented pharmacological responses that happen when the dose is too high or the patient is sensitive. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h3)

question: An unexpected, allergic reaction to a standard dose of penicillin is an example of which reaction type?
explanation: Bizarre reactions are unpredictable, immune-mediated responses that do not relate to the drug's normal pharmacological dose. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which agency handles drug safety monitoring across Nigeria?
explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control oversees drug safety, regulation, and post-market surveillance in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h4)

question: What paper form do Nigerian healthcare workers use to report suspected bad reactions to drugs?
explanation: The NAFDAC Yellow Form is the standard reporting instrument utilized for capturing suspected adverse drug reactions in local clinical settings. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the name of the global database used worldwide for international drug safety data?
explanation: VigiBase serves as the WHO global database repository for suspected adverse drug reactions gathered from member countries worldwide. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why do national agencies share local drug safety information with international organizations?

options.A: To allow foreign countries to manufacture local herbal products
options.B: To help detect rare safety signals across diverse global populations
options.C: To bypass local institutional ethical committee approvals
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of domestic clinical trials

explanation: Pooling data globally allows regulators to spot rare adverse events that might not appear in a single country alone. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h5)

question: A patient develops a sudden itchy rash shortly after starting a new antibiotic. What should you do first?

options.A: Ignore the rash because mild skin changes are normal side effects
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report it to the head nurse
options.C: Stop the infusion, notify the prescriber, and document the reaction
options.D: Increase the fluid infusion rate to flush the drug out quickly

explanation: Immediate cessation of the offending agent prevents severe anaphylaxis, followed by prompt notification and documentation. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why are nurses so important for spotting adverse drug reactions in the hospital?

options.A: They administer medications directly and observe immediate patient reactions
options.B: They possess the legal authority to withdraw unsafe drugs from markets
options.C: They manage the national drug manufacturing budget allocations
options.D: They design and execute pre-clinical laboratory animal trials

explanation: Nurses spend the most bedside time with patients, giving them a direct window to spot unexpected drug reactions. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the most common problem facing drug safety systems around the world?

options.A: Under-reporting of adverse drug reactions by clinicians
options.B: An excess of accurate digital data flooding agencies
options.C: Complete elimination of substandard medicines on markets
options.D: Excessive funding dedicated to local safety directorates

explanation: Most adverse drug reactions go undocumented because healthcare workers face heavy workloads and reporting apathy. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h7)

question: How can technology help improve drug safety monitoring in hospitals?

options.A: By removing the need for nurses to monitor patients at the bedside
options.B: By replacing government regulatory bodies with computer software
options.C: By guaranteeing that adverse drug reactions never happen again
options.D: By automatically analyzing health records to flag safety signals quickly

explanation: Electronic tools and algorithms can process large volumes of patient data rapidly to detect unexpected drug signals early. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h7)
